completeness.reason: Covers all 7 named export functions, compile returning function with .dependencies array, compileClient options (name, module), compileClientWithDependenciesTracked return shape, pug named properties (name/runtime/filters/cache), callback API semantics, caching behavior (cache+filename requirement), mixin support, register.js hook, and pipeline stages. Notable gap: whitespace-sensitive template syntax (if/else/each/while loops, inline code with -, attribute syntax, tag nesting) is identified as a capability but not described in the prompt. This matters because control flow rendering is tested in blackbox tests.

Cache object {} and filters object {} specified. compileClientWithDependenciesTracked return shape {body, dependencies} and options.module behavior documented. However, template syntax (how if/each/while render, how interpolation works, whitespace sensitivity) is not described at all, leaving a major implementation gap.

testability.reason: The prompt covers the API surface (compile, render, compileFile, renderFile, compileClient, cache, callbacks, named exports) which allows blackbox testing of structural properties. But control flow rendering (if/else, each with index, while, inline code) is heavily tested and not described in the prompt. An implementer would need prior pug knowledge to implement the template syntax correctly, reducing prompt-driven testability.

consistency.reason: No conflicts between stated behaviors and test expectations. pug.name='Pug' matches test. pug.runtime is non-null object matches test. pug.cache is {} matches test. compileClientWithDependenciesTracked returns {body, dependencies} matches test. dependencies is Array on compile function matches test.
